title: Modern methods and support processes
sub: Lecture 8 (second part) · Lean, TPS, Lean vs Six Sigma, TOC, ABC-XYZ, pull, JIT, JIS, Kanban, facility management, TPM
blurb: The theory block of Test 2 and the state exam: Lean and TPS, the 5 steps of TOC, how pull, JIT, JIS and Kanban fit together, and TPM.
lede: Mostly theory, asked as short definitions. The teacher listens for specific words: value and waste for Lean, variability for Six Sigma, exploit as the second step of TOC.
six: **Lean** increases **value** to the customer by reducing **waste** in a **continuous improvement** environment.
**TPS** has 14 principles in 4 sections: long-term philosophy · the right process · developing people and partners · solving root problems.
**Pull** is the philosophy, **JIT** makes only what's needed, **JIS** delivers it in assembly order, **Kanban** is the signal.
**TPM**: total, productive, maintenance. Goals: no defects, no unplanned downtime, no accidents.
foot: Sources: 3BE216 lecture slides 'Modern Methods and Support Processes' and the second half of Lecture 8 as recorded.

questions.answer: increases value to the customer by reducing waste, with continuous improvement
questions.e: Value, waste, continuous improvement: the three words.
If you answer without the word variability, you didn't answer.

questions.q: Craft, mass and lean production: which offers variety AND low cost?
questions.e: Craft: flexible but costly. Mass: cheap but little variety. Lean: both.

questions.answer: Base your management decisions on a long-term philosophy, even at the expense of short-term financial goals
wrong: Use a pull system to avoid overproduction

questions.q: 'Level out the workload (heijunka): work like the tortoise, not the hare' belongs to which TPS section?
questions.answer: 2P · the right process will produce the right results
questions.e: Principles 2–8: flow, pull, heijunka, stop to fix problems, standardised tasks, visual control, reliable technology.

questions.answer: go and see for yourself to understand the situation
questions.e: Principle 12, section 4P. Hansei = reflection, kaizen = continuous improvement.
The teacher: if you say 'make the bottleneck disappear' as step 2, you lose the points.

questions.q: The basic concepts of TOC are throughput, inventory and…
In ABC-XYZ, which items suit just in time best?
questions.answer: AX: high value, used very regularly
questions.e: High value means you don't want it in stock; regular use means the supply can flow.

questions.q: 'Give me what I need in the right time' describes…

questions.answer: make only what you need, when you need it, in the amount needed
questions.e: JIT is the first tool of pull.

questions.answer: parts arrive in the same order as the assembly sequence
a card or signal that tells the previous step to move or produce ('take one, make one')
questions.e: It controls the flow of resources.

questions.answer: the functionality of the built environment: people, place, process and technology
questions.e: The IFMA definition. Lifts, heating, cleaning, the building.
Total: everyone. Productive: without stopping production. Maintenance: equipment in good condition.

questions.q: The goals of TPM are no product defects, no unplanned downtime and…
questions.e: Bad maintenance of a window can break your hand.

questions.q: How are TPM and OEE linked?
questions.answer: The losses in OEE are what TPM tries to remove
wrong: TPM measures the price of machines
